Worldly life is only amusement and diversion, while the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah.
Worldly life is like rain that makes the earth bloom until, when its people think they control it, Allah's command makes it a harvest as if it never flourished.
Those who desire only this world's life and adornments are fully repaid in it, but in the Hereafter they have only the Fire, and what they did is lost.
Allah extends and restricts provision for whom He wills; people rejoice in the worldly life, though compared to the Hereafter it is only brief enjoyment.
Whoever wants the immediate may get some of it, then Hell, while the believer striving for the Hereafter is appreciated; Allah gives to both, but the Hereafter's ranks are greater.
Allah made the earth's adornment a test of who is best in deeds, and He will turn it into barren ground.
Worldly life is like rain-fed plants that dry into chaff scattered by the wind; wealth and children are its adornment, but lasting good deeds are better with your Lord.
Do not long for the worldly splendor given to some of them as a test, for your Lord's provision is better and more lasting.
Whatever people are given is enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with Allah is better and lasting; one promised good is not like one given worldly enjoyment then punished.
Worldly life is only diversion and amusement, while the home of the Hereafter is the true life.
Most people know only the outward side of worldly life and are unaware of the Hereafter.
Allah sends rain that flows as springs and grows crops of varied colors that dry, yellow and crumble, a parable of worldly life and a reminder for people of understanding.
Whoever seeks the harvest of the Hereafter is given more of it, while whoever seeks this world is given some of it but no share in the Hereafter.
Were it not that people would become one community, Allah would give disbelievers houses of silver and gold, yet that is worldly enjoyment, and the Hereafter is for the righteous.
Turn away from whoever ignores the message and wants only worldly life; that is all they know, and Allah knows best who strays and who is guided.
Worldly life is amusement, adornment, boasting, rivalry in wealth and children, withering like plants after rain; race toward Allah's forgiveness and a Garden as wide as the heavens and earth.
People prefer worldly life though the Hereafter is better and more lasting, as stated in the former scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
Competing for more distracts people until they visit the graves; they will surely see Hellfire with certainty and be asked that Day about their pleasures.
